newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: NAB says rate margins being squeezed.
newsitem.headline: NAB says rate margins being squeezed.

text.p: National Australia Bank Ltd (NAB) said on Thursday that its margins were down across the group, declining by 40 basis points due to increased competition in most areas of business.
The company earlier said its net half profit for the six months to March 31 rose 14.2 percent to A$1.14 billion, up from A$998 million in the previous corresponding half.
NAB said that despite declining margins, the group's net interest income increased by 3.6 percent over the previous first half due to rising volumes.

Within NAB's Australian unit, banking operations posted a 1.1 percent fall in earnings to A$631 million. But the unit's other contributors, National Australia Funds Management (NAFM) and BNZ Australia lifted the overall result to A$721 million, a rise of 1.4 percent.

The group's international performance was much stronger with bank's U.K.and Irish subsidiaries, Clydesdale Bank, Yorkshire Bank and Northern Bank lifting their overall net profit by 33.5 percent to A$215 million.
NAB said Bank of New Zealand's profit rose 31.3 percent to A$172 million and benefited from better lending volumes.
